##NOTE about how to use this script##

We have retained original code for merging in certain variables that we included as a part of the revision process. As such, lines 28-82 are not necessary to reproduce what we report in the manuscript. However, all of the files to execute these lines are available on our OSF page ("reversed_ANES_therm-data.csv", "sexuality_clean_IAT_county-revised.csv")

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

Load the packages that are needed to run the script
```{r}
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(tidyverse)
library(sjPlot)
library(sjlabelled)
library(sjmisc)
```

```{r}
setwd("your-working-directory-here")

#read in the data
d <- read_csv("completeIAT-and-control-data-SOpolicy_2022.04.26.csv")

#set penalty for printing numbers in scientific notation
options(scipen = 999)
```

Join updated gay/lesbian women explicit variable
```{r}
#read in updated variable
d.gayles <- read_csv("sexuality_clean_IAT_county-REVISED.csv") %>% 
  select(state = STATE, CountyNo, mean_exp_gayleswomen_combine, sd_exp_gayleswomen_combine, 
         mean_exp_straightwomen, sd_exp_straightwomen)

#create lesbian women bias score
d.gayles <- d.gayles %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(les_bias_diff_full = (mean_exp_straightwomen - mean_exp_gayleswomen_combine)) %>% 
  ungroup()

#drop straight women variable from gay/les women data because it is already present in the full data
d.gayles <- d.gayles %>% 
  select(-mean_exp_straightwomen, -sd_exp_straightwomen)

#pad leading zeroes on county variable so that the merging works
d$CountyNo <- str_pad(d$CountyNo, 3, side = "left", pad = "0")

#merge new variable with full data
d <- merge(d, d.gayles, by = c("state", "CountyNo"), sort = TRUE)

#create straight vs. gay relative preference index by combining explicit gay men bias and explicit lesbian women bias
d <- d %>%
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(exp_rel_pref = (gay_bias_diff + les_bias_diff_full)/2) %>% 
  ungroup()
```

Join ANES data
```{r}
#read data
d.anes <- read_csv("reversed_ANES_therm-data.csv") %>% 
  dplyr::select(state, ANES_exp_mean, ANES_N, ANES_SD)

#merge ANES data with full data
d <- merge(d, d.anes, by = "state", sort = TRUE)

#write data to csv
write_csv(d, file = "FINAL_OSF_sexualityIAT_2023.01.10.csv")
```

Load the data using your preferred method. The data file that corresponds with this script is named "FINAL_OSF_sexualityIAT_2023.01.10.csv" and is available on our OSF page.
```{r}
#read in final data file from OSF (this is the same file that was written in line 79 above)
d <- read_csv("FINAL_OSF_sexualityIAT_2023.01.10.csv")
```


Data preparation (e.g., renaming variables, creating mean-centered versions of predictors)
```{r}
#overwrite data
d <- d %>%
  #rename religiosity variable and census region
  rename(christians_per1k = cathrate_per1k,
         census_region = region) %>% 
  #log transform income variable and number of responses to IAT per county
  mutate(mean_income_allhouseholds_log = log(mean_income_allhouseholds),
         n_sexuality_IAT_log = log(n_sexuality_IAT)) %>% 
  #grand-mean center continuous variables
  mutate_at(vars(mean_exp_gaymen, mean_exp_gayleswomen_combine, mean_exp_straightmen, 
                 mean_exp_straightwomen, gay_bias_diff, les_bias_diff_full, exp_rel_pref, 
                 christians_per1k, percent_bachelorshigher, pop_ten_year_log,
                 mean_income_allhouseholds_log, IRR2010),
         list(cent = ~ . - mean(., na.rm = T))) %>% 
  #z transform variables
  mutate_at(vars(mean_imp_sexuality_bias, mean_exp_gaymen, mean_exp_gayleswomen_combine, mean_exp_straightmen, 
                 mean_exp_straightwomen, gay_bias_diff, les_bias_diff_full, exp_rel_pref,
                 christians_per1k, percent_bachelorshigher, pop_ten_year_log,
                 mean_income_allhouseholds_log, Republican_vote2016, IRR2010),
            list(z = ~ ((.) - mean(., na.rm = T)) / sd(., na.rm = T))) %>% 
  #rearrange columns so the order makes sense
  relocate(ends_with("_cent"), .after = n_all_IAT) %>% 
  relocate("christians_per1k", .after = Republican_vote2016) %>% 
  #create grand mean centered policy variable and ANES variable
  mutate(SO_policy_tally_gm = ((SO_policy_tally - mean(SO_policy_tally))),
         ANES_exp_mean_gm = ((ANES_exp_mean - mean(ANES_exp_mean))),
         #z transformed policy and ANES
         SO_policy_tally_z = ((SO_policy_tally - mean(SO_policy_tally)) / sd(SO_policy_tally, na.rm = T)),
          ANES_exp_mean_z = ((ANES_exp_mean - mean(ANES_exp_mean)) / sd(ANES_exp_mean, na.rm = T)))
```

#comparing US census and Williams Institute variables for same-gender couples

The following correlation matrix reports the correlations between all key study variables and the US census estimates of same-gender couples per county. These correlations can be compared against those reported in table 1 of the manuscript to compare between the US census estimates and the Williams Institute estimates. Generally, the US census correlations are in the same direction as those with the Williams Institute data, but of weaker magnitude.

```{r}
#zero order correlations
correlation_total2 <- d %>%
  dplyr::select(census_SS_HH = acs_samesex_hh_per1k, IAT_S = mean_imp_sexuality_bias, 
                EXP_GM = gay_bias_diff, EXP_LW = les_bias_diff_full, EXP_BIAS = exp_rel_pref, 
                EXP_ANES = ANES_exp_mean, POL = SO_policy_tally,
                CONS = Republican_vote2016, EDU = percent_bachelorshigher, 
                INC = mean_income_allhouseholds_log, REL = christians_per1k, RUR = IRR2010) %>% 
  drop_na()

#Making the correlation matrix
corr_total2 <- Hmisc::rcorr((as.matrix(correlation_total2)))

#print matrix
corr_total2
```

Regression comparing US census and Williams Institute same-gender households
```{r}
#model with census same-gender couples per 1k households as criterion and only aggregated sociodemographics as predictors
mod2_agg.dem_census <- lm(acs_samesex_hh_per1k ~ christians_per1k_z 
                                       + percent_bachelorshigher_z 
                                       + mean_income_allhouseholds_log_z 
                            + Republican_vote2016_z + IRR2010_z + as.factor(census_region), 
                                       weights = n_sexuality_IAT_log,
                                       na.action = na.omit,
    data = d)

#view model output
summary(mod2_agg.dem_census)


#model with williams same-gender couples per 1k households as criterion and only aggregated sociodemographics as predictors
mod2_agg.dem_williams <- lm(same_sex_per_1k ~ christians_per1k_z +
                                           percent_bachelorshigher_z +
                                           mean_income_allhouseholds_log_z + 
                                           Republican_vote2016_z +
                                           IRR2010_z + as.factor(census_region), 
                                       weights = n_sexuality_IAT_log,
                                       na.action = na.omit,
    data = d)

#view model output
summary(mod2_agg.dem_williams)

```

Gather additional details for method section (actual range of measures / number of counties with > 1000 Christian adherents per 1000 residents)
```{r}
#get data frame with limited variables to find min and max values for variables. Open d2 in data viewer and sort columns by ascending or descending.
d2 <- d %>% 
  select(County, state, n_sexuality_IAT, mean_imp_sexuality_bias, exp_rel_pref, gay_bias_diff, les_bias_diff, mean_income_allhouseholds, christians_per1k, Republican_vote2016, IRR2010, percent_bachelorshigher, ANES_exp_mean, SO_policy_tally)

#some counties have more than 1k christians per 1k population. We leave them in the data, as this could be due to
#undercounting of population, overcounting of religious adherents, or cross-county religious participation.

#list counties with greater than 1k christians per 1k population
d %>% 
  select(christians_per1k, state, County, CountyNo) %>% 
  filter(christians_per1k >= 1000) %>% 
  knitr::kable()
```

For each model, we attempted to use MLM but encountered model convergence failures. We retain the code to execute these models, but have commented out the code.

# Get correlation between state-level Project Implicit measures and ANES measure
```{r}
d.anes2 %>% 
  dplyr::select(ANES_exp_mean, mean_imp_sexuality_bias_state_mean, exp_rel_pref_state_mean) %>% 
  cor()

```
